annotation.title_clean: Towards Granting of Legal Personality to Autonomous Robots in the UAE
annotation.title_en: Towards Granting of Legal Personality to Autonomous Robots in the UAE
annotation.venue: International Journal of Innovation, Creativity and Change
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article examining whether autonomous robots can be granted legal personality under UAE law consistent with Islamic jurisprudence. It finds robots cannot be treated as mere things or full persons, and proposes partial or incomplete legal capacity, akin to minors, as a legislative solution.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous robots currently treated as movable things under UAE Civil Transactions Law Art. 102, with Art. 316 liability for things.
Autonomous robots cannot properly be classed as mere things nor as full persons.
Proposes partial or incomplete legal capacity, like minors, as a solution consistent with Islamic jurisprudence.
Draws on German 'partial legal capacity' theory and EU 2017 robotics rules.
Dubai AI ethics guidelines require accountability and may signal movement toward AI legal personality.
